selection_notes: Goal: real small-business copy, not chosen for quality and not memorable/famous. FRAME 1 (email, web, post, product-1): a deterministic walk of the Wayback CDX index of Mailchimp hosted campaign pages, https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=mailchi.mp/*&output=json&limit=400&to=2019&collapse=urlkey (200 text/html, captured 2017-2019). Rows are sorted by urlkey, i.e. by random hex campaign IDs, so the order is effectively random. Every row was screened in that order (downloads kept in raw/_cand and raw/_screen); skipped: non-business senders (nonprofits, churches, schools, associations, political groups, individuals, government projects), non-English emails, signup forms, and digests of third-party news (Netplus Marketing's 'Digital Bites', ConsenSys, Trivium China). EMAIL = the first three company emails about the sender's own business with a 120-400-word run of body copy: Greenco, Argo Bookshop, Oke USA/Equal Exchange (Natures Goodness store skipped: mostly link lists). WEB = the business senders met in the same walk, in order and not used elsewhere, whose homepage (latest real 200 capture <= 2019-12-31) has a hero + feature/benefit run of 120-400 words: Natures Goodness (homepage mostly partner CBD-brand copy, skipped), Netplus (post-merger homepage of case-study titles, skipped), Trivium China (web-1), Sunday Best Quiltworks (fragments/navigation, skipped), Tiny Type Museum (a single product, not SaaS/agency/local business; used as product), Swine Management Services (no archived site), Cosmic Smile Dental (web-2), Little Red Kitchen Bake Shop (mostly product grid), Beechwood Hotel (only run ends in a VisitEngland quote plus CMS-truncated teasers). web-3 was not filled within the time box. POST = same walk order; the newest post linked from the company's last-2019 homepage/blog index that has an archived capture and a 150-400-word body: Netplus Marketing (post-1), Sunday Best Quiltworks (post-2); Beechwood Hotel posts were 50-60 words; later walk businesses had no archived blog. post-3 not filled within the time box. PRODUCT = same walk order; the first product featured on the shop's last-2019 homepage with an archived page and a 100-300-word description: Sunday Best Quiltworks '7 Dancing Sisters' (84 words, skipped), Tiny Type Museum (product-1), Little Red Kitchen 'Elvis Cookie Pie' (40 words, skipped). Few walk senders run online shops, so FRAME 2 was used for the rest: the CDX prefix listing https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=etsy.com/listing/58&matchType=prefix&limit=400&from=2018&to=2019&collapse=urlkey taken in order, keeping English listings by sellers in English-speaking countries with a 100-300-word description: 580000111 Fandancyshop (product-2), 580000176 (snapshot could not be retrieved, skipped), 580000423 WeeMagicMarket (product-3). EXCERPT RULE: one contiguous run starting at the top of the body/hero/description and ending at the last complete section, paragraph or sentence that keeps it within the length limit; it stops before quoted third-party copy (publisher blurb, assessor quote, curated news); post excerpts are the body without title/byline. TEXT: verbatim output of tools/fetch_controls.py (html.parser; drops script/style/noscript/svg/nav/footer/button/iframe/select, hidden elements and cookie-banner elements; one block element per line; whitespace collapsed; zero-width characters removed); no edits or typo fixes. Anchors are the first/last ~8 words; matching treats any whitespace (including line breaks) between words as equal. All snapshots are 2018-2019 captures and the copy is dated 2018-2019 where a date is shown. All companies are small or medium (Equal Exchange is a mid-size worker co-op); none are famous brands or famous ads.
